primary: Number of distinct (expression, relation) laws among final claims with horizons all or interior that pass at least one comparison and all comparisons on both development and holdout, per arm and replicate. Nested horizon variants count once. No significance claim with two replicates.
baseline: Enumerate all 24 admitted claims without a model; freeze those passing development before inspecting holdout.
chronology: The investigators derived the k=2 additive four-point ordering and a candidate all-k extension before any model call. Neither direction nor proof is supplied to the model. The investigators selected the formula grammar and higher-k question. This pilot tests blinded rediscovery and selection of investigator-conjectured laws; it cannot credit the model with originating the grammar or either additive result.
interpretation: One shared initial model call per replicate, then one call per arm. Each arm logically uses two calls; the shared initial call is charged fully to each standalone arm and only once to actual total. All failures count, with no application retries or model/provider fallbacks; the gateway may internally retry within the selected provider. Feedback contains exact development counterexamples only. All final portfolios freeze before holdout. Passing finite cases is not a proof or a literature-first claim. Provider-reported usage excludes this coding/review session and mathematical proof work. Input cost reservation conservatively uses the entire advertised model context per dispatched call, plus the output cap. For k>2 the matching consequence concerns the expected number of intact pairs, not expected largest-component service. No billing changes or credits purchases.
